name: quasi88
why: A PC-8801 emulator opens a door into a forgotten Japanese 8-bit machine with real old-school software to explore.

brief.what_it_is: QUASI88 is a PC-8801 emulator, the Japanese 8-bit home computer from NEC. The homepage says it runs on Windows with SDL2 or on UNIX with SDL2, and it is described as an emulator for UNIX/X11+SDL. According to the Homebrew caveats, you supply the machine's ROM files and disk images, which it reads from ~/quasi88/rom/, ~/quasi88/disk/ and ~/quasi88/tape/ by default. The output is the emulated PC-8801 running in a window with sound. The homepage itself is in Japanese and does not describe the input and output formats in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. It presents QUASI88 as a free PC-8801 emulator and credits the fMSX source code as a reference for its design.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says the emulator was written with reference to fMSX source code. Its sound output section was ported from MAME and xmame, and it includes the fmgen FM sound generator by cisc. The homepage does not explain the emulation core in more detail.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, you need to place ROM and disk files yourself. The Homebrew caveats say the default directories are ~/quasi88/rom/, ~/quasi88/disk/ and ~/quasi88/tape/, and they can be overridden with -romdir, -diskdir and -tapedir. The caveats do not name the specific ROM files needed, and I did not reach the usage page to confirm them. SDL2 is a runtime dependency. Usage and download pages are linked from the homepage, but I did not fetch them.
brief.standout: It is a PC-8801 emulator that targets SDL2 on UNIX, which is unusual for this machine, and it borrows sound code from MAME and xmame and the fmgen FM generator. Its own copyright notice says the project is free software under a modified BSD license, with the sound output section governed by the MAME and xmame licenses.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage names 0.7.4 as the latest version, released 2026/05/01, and the copyright notice runs to 2026. I did not see a commit history or changelog to confirm the pace of development.
brief.caveats: The homepage is entirely in Japanese. Development is on Windows 11 and FreeBSD. Windows 10, Linux and macOS are reported to work, and the homepage says it should run on any platform SDL2 supports, but that is unverified. You must supply ROM and disk files yourself. The sound output section is under MAME and xmame licensing rather than the modified BSD license. The homepage disclaims all warranty and liability. I did not check the README or changelog in English.

QUASI88 は、fMSX のソースコードを参考にして、作成されました。

fetch_log: https://www.eonet.ne.jp/~showtime/quasi88/ - fetched OK, Japanese-language homepage. Its usage, download and features pages are linked but were not fetched because I did not have their URLs.

judge.reason: A focused emulator for the little-known Japanese PC-8801 lets you explore a distinct 8-bit computing platform and its original software.

entry.title: QUASI88
entry.tldr: An SDL2 emulator for NEC's PC-8801, a Japanese 8-bit home computer, so you can run its software in a window with sound.
entry.deeper_look:
QUASI88 emulates the PC-8801, an 8-bit home computer from NEC that was popular in Japan. It runs the machine in a window with sound. It targets SDL2 on UNIX and Windows, so it should work wherever SDL2 does.

The emulator does not ship with software. You supply the machine's ROM files and disk images yourself, and it looks for them in `~/quasi88/rom/`, `~/quasi88/disk/` and `~/quasi88/tape/`. The `-romdir`, `-diskdir` and `-tapedir` options point it elsewhere. The Homebrew caveats do not name which ROM files are required.

The homepage says the emulator was written with reference to the fMSX source code. Its sound output section was ported from MAME and xmame, and it includes the fmgen FM sound generator by cisc. That lineage is a way into how 8-bit machines were emulated and how their FM sound chips were reproduced in software.

The project is current: the homepage lists version 0.7.4, released 2026/05/01. The homepage is in Japanese only, which is part of the appeal and part of the effort.
entry.install:
brew install quasi88
# Then place your own ROM and disk files in ~/quasi88/rom/, ~/quasi88/disk/ and ~/quasi88/tape/
# Needs PC-8801 ROM files and disk images that you supply; SDL2 is pulled in as a dependency.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the available options, including the directory overrides for ROMs, disks and tapes.

entry.whats_unique: It is a PC-8801 emulator built on SDL2 for UNIX, which is an unusual target for this machine. It reuses sound code from MAME and xmame plus the fmgen FM generator.
entry.caveats: You must provide ROM and disk files yourself, the homepage is entirely in Japanese, and macOS and Linux support is reported but unverified by the author's main platforms (Windows 11 and FreeBSD).
